lines.text: It rained all night. For the first time in nineteen days, that was good news. Oakhaven. Day nineteen. The greenhouse won. Five votes. Weston went back to Hollow Creek and pulled every unbroken pane of glass off that greenhouse. They carried them home one at a time, and Weston framed them in scrap wood. There's a greenhouse in the corner of the yard now. Mateen moved half his seedlings in before the glass was even dry. Food, every night, from now on. And the rain kept coming. Every barrel on every roof filled by morning. Twenty-two rations of water, caught out of the sky, thanks to the engineers who built the rain catchers. Artemis, Frost, Kim, Hudson, and Johnny. Francis is back on his feet. Steve is still on a cot with his shoulder strapped. That night, Elias sat by the burn barrel in a wet coat, his collar still buttoned all the way up. He was sweating, even in the cold. When someone asked if he was feeling all right, he waved it off. "Too many cold nights on that roof," he said. "I'll be fine." Later, at supper, he got up without saying a word, walked over to Steve lying on his cot, and gave him his dinner. Forty-three of us. Even with the rain, food and water only last one more day. And the horde reaches the fence in two. Where do we go tomorrow? The army surplus store, easy, never searched. The air freight yard, bigger, and more ways to get caught. Or the fire truck, with Frost, for the rest of the water. Comment your name and your job, to move in.
